rationale: Link the trim child to the snapshot receipt that answers the first half of its discriminator, and narrow the parent's reconfiguration-handoff item by source. The trim interpretation now records that a second producer (the snapshot path) reaches over-compaction, that this producer needs only the drifted decided index rather than any recorded accepted index, and that the earlier bounds still hold; the parent's discriminator drops the handoff item to a sourced narrowing because the library's own handoff carries only the next configuration and its metadata in the StopSign while the documented flow builds the new instance with fresh storage and requires the user to supply the application state, so a drifted index does not transfer through the library.

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed and bounded, now with a second producer recorded. The trim witness stands: with recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content and every node's decided report at 9, trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7, past the leader's own content, after which its reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15). The discriminator this question carried asked whether a producer other than trim can raise a compacted index past a replica's content, and the snapshot receipt answers that it can: with the same drifted state, snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the leader's compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). That second producer is stricter in one respect and looser in another than trim: it needs no recorded accepted index at all - its bound is the leader's decided index - so a drift confined to the decided index would be enough for it, while trim additionally needs the drifted value to be the configuration's minimum recorded accepted index. What remains bounded from the earlier reading: both producers are bounded by values the leader derives for itself, so a replica whose recorded report is still truthful keeps trim's bound honest (the minimum) and the snapshot witness also required the leader's own decided index to have drifted; and no in-cluster promise or log sync in the observed runs asked for a prefix below a compacted index, so the storage underflow I had sourced from the lead was not triggered.
counterevidence: Every node's decided report had also drifted to 9, so the documented all-decided precondition was satisfied only in the drifted bookkeeping; the obligation I rely on is that the compacted index must not exceed the entries the leader holds, which it did (7 for trim, 8 for the snapshot).
The trim call returned Ok, so nothing in its own result signals the over-compaction; the witness is the compacted index together with the content sampled before and after.

The crash path is argued unreachable in this configuration rather than merely untested: the trim bound is the minimum recorded accepted index, so every replica's recorded value is at or above the compacted index and no in-cluster suffix request can fall below it.
limitations: The trim over-compaction is bounded to replicas whose recorded accepted index has drifted; a truthful replica would have kept the bound lower.

The underflow remainder is a property of a storage or caller that requests a prefix below the compacted index by another route; other storage implementations may differ and the trait leaves out-of-range behaviour to the implementer.
The baseline comparisons of both receipts are unknown because they were admitted through event names shared across cases in one execution; those states are asserted from the sampled operands.

One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one leader change (trim) and one snapshot-capable entry type were exercised; forwarded compaction on the peers was not sampled beyond their accepted and decided indexes.

knowledge.assertion: trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
trim's bound is the minimum recorded accepted index, so a truthful replica keeps it honest

investigations.discriminator: Whether the drift is bounded by anything inside the sealed configuration (a counter or storage limit, or a repair triggered by a later leader change), whether it transfers through the library's own reconfiguration handoff (narrowed: the StopSign carries only the next configuration and metadata while the documented flow builds the new instance with fresh storage and requires the user to supply the application state), and whether further producers of compaction exist; the decisive observations would be the reported indexes after many more rounds, a later leader change, and any compaction path not yet exercised.
